name: Adaptive Rank Selection via Binary Search
definition: A method to adaptively determine the optimal Tucker decomposition rank (R1, R2, R3) for each data block in multi-resolution volume rendering. It solves the trade-off between compression ratio and reconstruction error (PSNR) by finding the smallest rank that satisfies a specific error threshold, avoiding the inefficiency of uniform high-rank decomposition or the quality loss of uniform low-rank decomposition.
summary: Adaptive Rank Selection via Binary Search determines optimal Tucker decomposition ranks per volume block by using binary search on pre-computed decompositions to balance compression and error, unlike uniform rank methods.
